prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Regional Dispatch Center (Juniper) continuously intakes emergency-medical requests, supports triage, dispatches ambulances, coordinates jurisdictions, and maintains incident/unit/access awareness under approved protocols. Call Taker Mara obtains details, confirms location, and enters requests via Computer Aided Dispatch Console, the primary assessment/dispatch workstation. Triage Supervisor reviews incidents, confirms priority, and directs clinical review. Regional Medical Director establishes clinical policies/delegation limits; dispatch personnel apply protocols and seek guidance beyond authority.
Shift Commander (Sundial) controls coordination/continuity, resolves conflicts, prioritizes surges, and escalates beyond-center decisions to jurisdictional leadership; authority does not override clinical-policy authority or Paramedic Crew on-scene judgment. Paramedic Crew assesses/treats within scope/protocols. Jurisdictions retain resource ownership/local-policy responsibility; regional service coordinates agreed responses.
Ambulance Coordination Platform supports incident, assignment, and resource-status views. Ambulance Unit 417 joins the response pool when assigned. Hospital Liaison Desk coordinates receiving capacity/destination constraints; Emergency Department communicates receiving considerations through regional procedures. Riverside Trauma Center suitability/availability follows protocols.
Response zones reflect distance, road access, and ambulance capacity; boundaries are maintained with jurisdictions and reviewed following road-network, population, or agreement changes. Each has primary/alternate routes to Emergency Department and Riverside Trauma Center, subject to clinical direction/access. Dispatch considers travel time, restrictions, weather, closures; crews verify constrained-route conditions before commitment.
North Gate Status Board presents northern access/queues and produces North Approach Queue Snapshot; South Gate Status Board presents southern access/ambulance-entry restrictions. Check both at shift start and relevant reported changes.
Radio Coordinator (Mistral) monitors/manages Regional Radio Network responder communications; confirms channel availability/backup-procedure understanding each shift. Radio checks verify weak-area coverage and detect problems before demand rises.
Fleet Maintenance Cell (Bluejay) monitors availability, servicing, defects/constraints; produces Battery Swap Voucher authorizing/documenting replacement. Readiness checks confirm staffing, communications, clinical supplies, fuel, condition, recorded maintenance restrictions.
Data Quality Officer reviews dispatch-record completeness, consistency, information-handling compliance.

New part:
S044: The Ambulance Coordination Platform provides a shared operational view of zone coverage and unit availability.
S045: The Computer Aided Dispatch Console supports dispatch work, while operational staff remain responsible for verifying that displayed information is current.
S046: The Shift Commander reviews readiness concerns that may require repositioning resources or adjusting local coverage plans.
S047: The Triage Supervisor coordinates clinical prioritization with dispatch operations when demand or access conditions change.
S048: The Paramedic Crew reports new access barriers and vehicle readiness concerns through established communications procedures.
S049: The Regional Dispatch Center compares reported conditions with current zone coverage and escalates unresolved readiness gaps to the appropriate operational lead.
S050: Readiness status is reassessed after significant incidents, service interruptions, or changes to routes and access conditions.
S051: The Regional Dispatch Center handles incoming emergency calls through a controlled intake process that creates an incident record for coordination.
S052: Call Taker Mara is also known by the radio alias Larkspur.
S053: The Hospital Liaison Desk is also known by the coordination alias Kestrel.
S054: Call Taker Mara establishes the caller's location before collecting medical details.
S055: Call Taker Mara asks for the street address, municipality, and any building, floor, or entrance information needed to find the patient.
S056: Call Taker Mara confirms the location by repeating the address and checking it against the caller's description of nearby landmarks.
S057: Call Taker Mara asks whether the caller can provide a callback number in case the connection is lost.
S058: Call Taker Mara gathers the patient's age, level of consciousness, breathing status, and the main reason emergency help is needed.
S059: Call Taker Mara uses direct questions to distinguish observed symptoms from information reported by someone else.
S060: Call Taker Mara records the time symptoms began when the caller can provide a reliable estimate.
S061: Call Taker Mara notes access barriers such as locked entrances, restricted roads, or difficulty reaching the patient.
S062: Call Taker Mara produces the Caller Location Correction Slip when the caller's address needs documented clarification.
S063: The Computer Aided Dispatch Console checks entered location details against available address and map data.
S064: If the location does not resolve cleanly, Call Taker Mara asks focused follow-up questions and updates the incident record.
S065: Call Taker Mara remains engaged with the caller when further information could change the response priority or access plan.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
